newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO no comment on Czech bank talk.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO no comment on Czech bank talk.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Wednesday it had no comment on a report it was interested in taking a significant stake in Investicni a Postovni Banka, one of the four largest banks in the Czech Republic.
Czech news agency CTK, quoting the private TV Nova news programme, said ABN AMRO management had confirmed the Dutch bank's interest in IPB, in which the Czech state has a 31.5 percent stake.
But ABN AMRO spokesman Tanno Massar said: "We classify this as market rumours. It's the kind of story that we don't want to comment on."
TV Nova said ABN AMRO had at least the same chance of buying into the bank as Japanese investment bank Nomura and Dutch group ING Groep NV.
Czech officials have confirmed Nomura and ING have expressed interest in the Czech state's 31.5 percent stake in IPB.
The Czech central bank and and finance ministry have called for the rapid privatisation of this shareholding to a strategic foreign partner.
ABN AMRO recently took an 89.23 percent stake in Hungary's Magyar Hitel Bank (MHB) for $89.23 million in an expansion of its eastern European operations.
